title: Article 109 — Special procedure in respect of Money Bills

content.overview: Article 109 provides the special procedure for Money Bills: a Money Bill may be introduced only in the House of the People; after passage by the Lok Sabha it is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha for recommendations; the Rajya Sabha must return it within 14 days with or without recommendations; the Lok Sabha may accept or reject any recommendations; the Bill is deemed passed by both Houses with the amendments (if any) accepted by the Lok Sabha. If the Rajya Sabha does not return the Bill within 14 days, it is deemed passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Lok Sabha.
content.glance: Money Bill: only in Lok Sabha. RS has 14 days for recommendations only (no veto). LS may accept or reject recommendations. Deemed passage if RS does not return in time.
content.study:
Article 109 special procedure:

1. Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Council of States.
2. After passage by the House of the People, transmitted to the Council of States for its recommendations.
3. Council of States must within 14 days return the Bill with or without recommendations.
4. House of the People may accept or reject all or any of the recommendations.
5. Bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses with the amendments (if any) accepted by the House of the People.
6. If not returned within 14 days, deemed passed by both Houses in the form passed by the House of the People.

Definition of Money Bill: Article 110.

Certification: Speaker’s certificate that a Bill is a Money Bill is final (Article 110(3)).

Examination: only LS introduction; RS recommendatory role only; 14-day window; LS dominance; deemed passage.

sections.heading: Procedure steps
sections.body:
1. Introduction only in Lok Sabha.
2. Transmission to Rajya Sabha for recommendations.
3. 14 days to return with/without recommendations.
4. Lok Sabha accepts or rejects recommendations.
5. Deemed passed by both Houses accordingly; or deemed passed if not returned in time.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the special procedure for Money Bills under Article 109.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 109, a Money Bill may be introduced only in the House of the People. After the Lok Sabha passes it, it is sent to the Rajya Sabha for recommendations. The Rajya Sabha must return it within 14 days with or without recommendations. The Lok Sabha may accept or reject any recommendations. The Bill is then deemed passed by both Houses with the amendments (if any) accepted by the Lok Sabha. If the Rajya Sabha does not return the Bill within 14 days, it is deemed passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Lok Sabha.
